scope: Determine whether the publicly indexed Kay-Alamang Estuary juvenile-fish diet presentation exposes a primary paper or species-level, site-resolved and reusable data suitable for the Bangwit research ledger. This is an access and evidence-scope review, not a diet or occurrence assertion.

method.publicSource: Opened the Biodiversity PH YouTube video abstract and reviewed its title, channel metadata and description. The description attributes the presentation to Dan David B. Vale Cruz and Dickson N. Dimero of Cavite State University Don Severino de las Alas Campus.
boundedSearches: Exact title with both named authors
Kay-Alamang with Leiognathidae and the reported prey groups
method.searchOutcome: The bounded public search returned the video abstract and contextual water-quality material, but no accessible primary article, thesis record, species table, supplement or data deposit for this fish-diet study.
method.dateCheck: YouTube metadata gives publication date 2020-08-11, before the 2020-08-22/23 forum dates stated in the video description. Public event listings and the Biodiversity PH forum recordings support the later forum dates. The earlier upload could be an advance/pre-recorded submission; no program slot or explanation was found. Neither date is a field-sampling date.
method.localRetention: No video, transcript, paper, image or data file was downloaded or retained. No account, private link, access-control workaround or direct inquiry was used.

findings: The video description identifies the study area as Kay-Alamang Estuary in Naic, Cavite and says the study used stomach-content analysis of juvenile fishes alongside zooplankton sampling.

The description reports four fish families (Leiognathidae, Ambassidae, Bothidae and Terapontidae) and nine zooplankton orders or grouped larval categories. It gives family-level prey-group summaries, not fish species names or a fish-to-prey specimen table.

The public description does not expose fish sample counts, capture dates, sampling stations, vouchers, specimen images, complete methods, exact locality geometry or the underlying primary paper. Family-level summaries cannot be assigned to individual species or generalized to adult fish or other waterbodies.

The title and description make this a potentially relevant estuarine food-web retrieval lead, but its available public representation is not sufficient to add species-level diet content, occurrence records or a current local checklist.

rightsReview.assessment: No item-specific license or reuse permission was found. The YouTube description states that video content, including images and data, is the property and responsibility of the authors. Public playback does not establish permission to reproduce the underlying data or figures.
rightsReview.disposition: Retain only attributed bibliographic metadata and concise research findings. Do not copy the video, images, underlying data or verbatim transcript.

decision.disposition: Add the video abstract as a research-only source-access lead. Keep family-level statements out of Bangwit's species diet feature until a traceable primary source provides species-level evidence, sample context and acceptable reuse terms.

limitations: A bounded search that did not locate the primary paper does not prove that the paper or data are unavailable elsewhere.
The video description is an author-attributed secondary presentation record; its family-level summary is not independently verified against the underlying paper or specimens.
The reported date conflict remains unresolved and no field collection period is known.
No fishing permission, current species presence, abundance, access, safety, catchability or bait recommendation is established.
nextActions: Continue searching public CvSU repository, journal and conference-archive records for the full paper or its tables, without treating the video description as a substitute.

If a full paper or dataset becomes publicly available, review fish identifications, juvenile life stage, sample dates and stations, specimen/voucher trail, fish-to-prey crosswalk, source lineage and item-specific reuse terms before extracting any claim.
Continue the separate CALABARZON inland-water sweep; this lead does not complete Naic, Cavite or the regional freshwater/brackish baseline.
